sources.title: J.S. Milne, Algebraic Geometry (Version 6.10)
sources.locator: Table of contents entries for Chapters 2-3 (PDF pp. 2-3); Chapter 2 §a `Definition of an algebraic set` (printed p. 36), §c `The Zariski topology` (printed pp. 38-39), §d `The Hilbert Nullstellensatz` and §e `The correspondence between algebraic sets and radical ideals` through Corollary 2.17 and the Galois-correspondence paragraph 2.23 (printed pp. 39-43), §g `Properties of the Zariski topology` and §h `Decomposition of an algebraic set into irreducible algebraic sets` through Proposition 2.31 and Corollary 2.32 (printed pp. 44-46), §i `Regular functions; the coordinate ring of an algebraic set` through Definition 2.38 (printed pp. 47-49), and Chapter 3 §c `The ringed space structure on an algebraic set` from Definition 3.8 through Corollary 3.12 together with §e `Affine algebraic varieties` and §g `Explicit description of morphisms of affine varieties` through Proposition 3.25 (printed pp. 60-67).

contents.name: a. Definition of an algebraic set
2.23, the Galois correspondence paragraph for I and V
Proposition 2.26(a)
contents.reason: The page keeps the T1 fact in the background and uses a concrete affine-line counterexample for non-Hausdorff behavior instead of scaffolding a separate general closed-point theorem here.

contents.name: Proposition 2.26(c)
contents.reason: Quasi-compactness of classical Zariski spaces becomes structurally important only once sheaves and gluing are abstracted later. This pair records principal opens and localization instead of isolating quasi-compactness as its own item.

contents.name: 2.34, noetherian Hausdorff spaces are finite
contents.reason: The page needs only the specific warning that the affine-line Zariski topology is coarse. It does not generalize that warning into a separate abstract noetherian-Hausdorff theorem before scheme theory begins.

contents.name: i. Regular functions; the coordinate ring of an algebraic set
the paragraph identifying k[V] with the polynomial functions on V
the paragraph sending radical ideals of k[V] to algebraic subsets of V
Definition 2.38
contents.reason: The next affine-varieties page explicitly owns the general definition of regular maps and the anti-equivalence with k-algebra homomorphisms. AV-1 uses only polynomial functions and the principal-open localization seam.

contents.name: Proposition 3.9
contents.reason: The full sheaf property for regular functions on arbitrary opens is a deliberate AV-2 item. This pair keeps only the principal-open localization theorem that the later sheaf proof depends on.

contents.name: Corollary 3.12
contents.reason: Local rings at points are owned by AV-2 together with germs and rational maps. AV-1 stops at principal-open sections and does not yet scaffold stalks or localizations at maximal ideals.

contents.name: Proposition 3.24
contents.reason: This is the full morphism-versus-homomorphism theorem. The next page owns that proof and the categorical consequences, while the present page only previews the object-side affine dictionary.

sources.title: Donu Arapura, Notes on Basic Algebraic Geometry
sources.locator: Contents page (PDF p. 2); Chapter 1 §1.1 from the opening definition of V(f) and Lemma 1.1.1 through the definition of algebraic set (PDF p. 3); §1.2 `Weak Nullstellensatz` (PDF pp. 5-7); §1.3 `Zariski topology` (PDF pp. 7-9); §1.5 `Affine Varieties` (PDF pp. 10-11); and §1.6 `Hilbert’s Nullstellensatz` through Theorem 1.6.5 (PDF pp. 11-12).

contents.name: Lemma 1.1.1
contents.reason: The page does not isolate the nonemptiness of the zero set of one nonconstant polynomial as its own theorem. Later proofs instead cite the published Nullstellensatz package and root-counting facts only where they are actually needed.

contents.name: Lemma 1.2.1
contents.reason: This page does not scaffold a separate theorem about the evaluation homomorphism on all of affine space. It uses the coordinate-ring quotient directly when identifying polynomial functions on an algebraic set.

contents.name: the cofinite-topology paragraph on the nonempty open sets of A^1
Lemma 1.3.4
contents.reason: Continuity of regular maps and the general regular-function language belong to the next affine page, which introduces morphisms and local quotient representatives on arbitrary opens.
